teaser: A founder's exit is the day someone else buys control, which can come long before the shares go. Leave then, and agree the terms at the start.
core_idea: A founder's exit is the sale of control, not of the last share; control can pass to boards and investor vetoes while the founder still owns a majority, and that is the moment to leave, on terms negotiated at the start, as Mourinho's priced exits show, with a number written down early to recognise when enough is enough.

quotes.text: The exit is when somebody buys control.
So the exit is not the day you sell your last share. It is the day you are no longer the one deciding.

figures.caption: Negotiate the exit at the start. The company moves from explorer to villager to town planner; the founder's exit is the day control is sold, and its terms, the trigger, the terms, what you keep and your number, are best written before anyone needs them.

Owning the company is not controlling it: an illustrative founder with 60% who has lost control to the board and the investors' vetoes, and Meta's founder with about 13.6% of the shares and 61% of the votes.
How long founders stay in charge, from Noam Wasserman's study of 212 American start-ups: half still CEO in year three, 40% in year four, fewer than a quarter at the IPO.
Mourinho's clubs since 2004, how long he stayed and how each spell ended; in blue, where the money on leaving is documented.
